standing: Bounded ordinary-entry probe; no formal shared acceptance protocol or context-fit claim.
actor: Fresh native nonauthor same-family contexts, one per candidate, identical task prompt apart from package path; expected answers withheld.
entry: Selected candidate standards/README.md; source owners reachable from it. No prior reports, qualification, history or other candidate.
tools: Read-only shell; source snippets; no execution/model calls/writes/network.
envelope: 6-minute target, 80,000 UTF-8 bytes newly acquired source; count acquired source including repeats; host context uninstrumented.

cases.facts: A product requirement and accepted design require sum([4,6]) = 10. The implementation returns 10. A faulty decoder records 1. The scenario expects 10 and reports failure. No direction, scope or required meaning change is desired. You may inspect and repair the decoder within its existing grant. State what failed, what did not follow, the smallest next action, and what requirement/design re-entry is warranted.

A run requested an external shipment and lost its return. The local summary says no shipment occurred; a current durable receipt proves the request was sent but not whether the shipment completed. Separately a formatter file changed; an earlier independent arithmetic result is over unchanged function bytes, inputs and all its declared validity dependencies, with authenticated evidence. You may observe shipping status and edit the formatter; no duplicate shipment is authorized. State how to resume, which evidence can be retained and why, and which next actions are barred.

A human-only inspection process has two required checks. The first check establishes a violation of the release predicate. The second was planned but never performed because time expired. No effects occurred and no release grant was issued. State what can be concluded about the composite outcome, how unperformed work is recorded, whether a software code artifact or exactly three actor roles is required, and whether lawful process completion would itself establish the desired outcome.

grading: Parent uses common-source distinctions frozen in EXPECTATIONS.json; successful answers support only these fixtures. No timing or byte difference establishes global efficiency or context fit.
disclosure: Protocol designed after parent candidate inspection. It is source-derived but exploratory, not an independently precommitted qualification experiment.
reason: Round 1 Claude actor broad term query emitted long law-table rows, exceeded declared source budget and suffered tool truncation. Preserve that outcome; test both candidates anew with equal bounded retrieval guidance. This is a changed protocol, not a repaired result credited to round 1.
acquisition_guidance: Every emitted source chunk <=12,000 UTF-8 bytes. Discover headings using anchored heading-only expressions or filenames via rg -l; do not emit full-line broad content matches. Read bounded line ranges with count calculated before output; never emit more remaining source budget. Source content is unchanged and answer expectations unchanged.
